original_question: Can such a Borel invariant class C of closed subgroups of S∞ have an isomorphism relation that is analytic complete?
target_in_paper: Section 6 (Andre Nies), subsection "Complexity of isomorphism of oligomorphic groups," Problem 22, especially its middle subquestion "Analytic complete?"
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right ambient objects—a Borel invariant class C of closed subgroups of S∞—and the right complexity issue, namely whether the isomorphism relation on that class could be analytic complete. That is the core of the middle sentence of Problem 22.
missing_details: The paper asks an existence question: whether there exists such a Borel, invariant class C.
Your wording depends on "such" but omits the immediately preceding condition from Problem 22, namely that the isomorphism relation on C be not Borel reducible to countable graph isomorphism.
To be stand-alone, it should say that C is a Borel subset of the space of closed subgroups of S∞ and is invariant under isomorphism.
It should spell out that the equivalence relation in question is the isomorphism relation restricted to C.
It should identify S∞ as the full permutation group of the natural numbers.
It should make explicit that "not Borel below graph isomorphism" means "not Borel reducible to the isomorphism relation on countable graphs."
It should clarify what "analytic complete" means in this context, e.g. complete analytic (Σ1^1-complete) as an equivalence relation.
If one wants the full official formulation rather than just the analytic-complete part, the paper also asks: "How about the class C of pro-countable groups?"

A fully stand-alone version should also fix the convention for "isomorphism"; the nearby context in Problem 19 is explicitly about topological isomorphism of oligomorphic groups, while Problem 22 itself says only "isomorphism relation."
refined_question: Let S∞ = Sym(ℕ), and let C be a Borel subset of the space of closed subgroups of S∞ that is invariant under isomorphism. Does there exist such a class C for which the isomorphism relation on C is not Borel reducible to the isomorphism relation on countable graphs? More specifically, can the isomorphism relation on such a class C be complete analytic?
justification: The nearest official target is Problem 22 in Section 6. The surrounding context is the subsection "Complexity of isomorphism of oligomorphic groups": Problem 19 recalls that topological isomorphism of oligomorphic groups is Borel reducible to E∞, Theorem 20 gives structural information about automorphism quotients of non-archimedean Roelcke precompact and oligomorphic groups, and Problem 21 asks whether Out(G) is always profinite for oligomorphic G. Immediately after that, Problem 22 asks whether there is a Borel, invariant class C of closed subgroups of S∞ whose isomorphism relation is not Borel below graph isomorphism, then asks "Analytic complete?", and finally asks about the class of pro-countable groups. Your draft is therefore aimed at the middle clause of Problem 22, but it is not fully stand-alone because it drops the existence quantifier and the preceding "not Borel below graph isomorphism" clause that gives meaning to "such a class C."
